record_body:
Account summary (regulated / insurer):
- Prospect is an EU-headquartered insurance group evaluating Redwood for internal claims + policy servicing copilots (RAG + summarization). They have budget allocated but will only transact via AWS Marketplace.
- Primary requirement theme: they need written, reviewable language for audit logs, retention controls, and EU data residency. They explicitly said they’ve been burned by “marketing security claims” and want precise, scoped statements.

Key contacts (as captured so far):
- VP Platform Engineering (economic buyer for infra) + Head of Security/GRC (gatekeeper) + Procurement (marketplace process owner).
- They’re also looping in their Data Protection Officer for residency + retention language.

Use case / workload notes:
- Workload: document search + summarization over internal PDFs and case notes; interactive chat with citations.
- Expected scale (their estimate): pilot 50–100 internal users, then 2k–5k users if approved; heavy weekday usage.
- Latency target: <2s first token for chat; <8s for long-form summaries (2–4 pages).
- Preference: private/VPC for the pilot due to “policyholder data concerns,” but they asked if Dedicated is acceptable as interim if isolated.
- Models: open to curated open models; they care about deterministic routing/fallback and version pinning for compliance.

Security / compliance requirements (verbatim-ish snippets):
- “We need audit logs we can actually use in investigations—who did what, when, from where.”
- “Retention needs to be configurable, and we need a statement on how long logs are kept by default vs optional extended retention.”
- “EU residency is not a preference. It’s a requirement.”
- They asked about encryption at rest, KMS, key ownership options, and whether private deployment supports customer-managed KMS.
- SSO/SAML required for Console access; also asked about SCIM.

Marketplace procurement notes:
- They want AWS Marketplace purchase mapped to a specific Redwood org + specific region; they flagged concern about “wrong account / wrong org” issues.
- Need a clean SKU story: base (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) + add-ons (retention/compliance/premium SLA). Procurement asked for SKU names exactly as they will appear on invoice.
- They asked if upgrades/downgrades are allowed mid-term via marketplace, or require a new private offer.

Activity timeline (recent):
- 2026-01-10: Inbound via referral; asked directly for AWS Marketplace path + security docs. (Owner: Jordan)
- 2026-01-16: Discovery call w/ SE (Markus) + platform lead. Notes reference Fireflies ff-9057 (marketplace purchase preference, VPC requirement).
- 2026-01-22: Shared Marketplace Security FAQ (draft) + high-level architecture slide; they replied with a list of required edits (audit logging scope, retention durations, residency statement).
- 2026-02-03: Security packet internal review referenced (Fireflies ff-9050) to tighten wording; Marcus Lin flagged removing ambiguous claims like “full audit logging of all customer actions” and replacing with scoped language.
- 2026-02-11: Customer security questionnaire received (28 questions). Biggest deltas were: data residency phrasing, retention and deletion controls, and whether logs can be exported.
- 2026-02-21: Procurement ping: won’t initiate AWS Marketplace order until they have an updated packet + explicit EU residency paragraph approved by their DPO.

Current requirements to unblock procurement (internal checklist):
- Provide buyer-facing security language that matches our actual controls:
  - Audit logging: what is logged (Console/admin events, entitlement/provisioning events, API access logs where applicable), where logs live, and how to export.
  - Retention controls: default retention window + availability of extended retention add-on; clarify which artifacts are impacted (logs, traces, usage analytics).
  - Residency: which regions supported for processing; clarify that model inference traffic stays in-region when configured; include subprocessor statement and any exceptions (support access) with approvals.
- Confirm AWS Marketplace SKU alignment:
  - Redwood Private (VPC) base + Retention Controls add-on + Premium SLA (if available).
  - Invoice-friendly descriptions (procurement requested “no acronyms”).

Risks / watch-outs:
- Very sensitive to over-promising. They will compare listing language to the security packet and to contractual terms.
- If we cannot provide EU-only processing statement that their DPO accepts, they will fall back to Bedrock.

Internal notes / owner reminders:
- Route any final security language through Dr. Aisha Rahman sign-off (Gmail thread-5c21aa10) and technical accuracy check with Marcus Lin (thread-1142cc9a).
- Use the approved phrasing from the Marketplace Security FAQ; avoid adding net-new claims in email.
- Confirm whether they need dedicated support routing / escalation language (premium SLA add-on) for procurement.
